k.tx: Usually where the water line enters the house, or at the meter near the street. Find it and label it before you need it, as Pinellas County advises.

k.tx: My water heater sat in storm flood water. Can I use it?
k.n: My water heater sat in storm flood water. Can I use it?

k.tx: Don’t turn it on. A heater that sat in flood water, salt water above all, usually needs replacing. Call and we check it first.
k.n: Don’t turn it on. A heater that sat in flood water, salt water above all, usually needs replacing. Call and we check it first.

k.tx: Tank or tankless for a Florida home?
k.n: Tank or tankless for a Florida home?

k.tx: It depends on how much hot water you use at once and whether you have gas. Tankless heats on demand and hangs on the wall. A tank stores hot water and costs less to fit.
k.n: It depends on how much hot water you use at once and whether you have gas. Tankless heats on demand and hangs on the wall. A tank stores hot water and costs less to fit.

k.tx: Do I need a permit to replace a water heater?
k.n: Do I need a permit to replace a water heater?

k.tx: Usually, yes. Pinellas County lists a “Water Heater Equal Change Out, Tank or Tankless” permit, and Clearwater requires permits for water heaters. We file it for you.
k.n: Usually, yes. Pinellas County lists a “Water Heater Equal Change Out, Tank or Tankless” permit, and Clearwater requires permits for water heaters. We file it for you.

k.tx: Source · pinellas.gov Express Permits · myclearwater.com, read 17 Nov 2026
k.n: Source · pinellas.gov Express Permits · myclearwater.com, read 17 Nov 2026

k.tx: How fast can you put in a new one?
k.n: How fast can you put in a new one?

k.tx: Often the next day. One customer wrote: “called and had one installed the next day”.
k.n: Often the next day. One customer wrote: “called and had one installed the next day”.

k.tx: How hard is Pinellas County water?
k.n: How hard is Pinellas County water?

k.tx: Very hard. It averages 217 ppm, which is 11.1 to 14.3 grains per gallon. That builds scale inside tanks and tankless units.
k.n: Very hard. It averages 217 ppm, which is 11.1 to 14.3 grains per gallon. That builds scale inside tanks and tankless units.

k.tx: Source · Pinellas County Utilities 2025 water quality report
k.n: Source · Pinellas County Utilities 2025 water quality report

k.tx: What should my softener be set to?
k.n: What should my softener be set to?

k.tx: Pinellas County Utilities gives 11.1 to 14.3 grains per gallon as the softener setting. We set it up when we install.
k.n: Pinellas County Utilities gives 11.1 to 14.3 grains per gallon as the softener setting. We set it up when we install.

k.tx: Source · Pinellas County Utilities 2025 water quality report

k.tx: Why does my water smell like a pool some weeks?
k.n: Why does my water smell like a pool some weeks?

k.tx: Twice a year Pinellas County Utilities switches from chloramine to free chlorine for a short time. The smell is that switch, not your pipes.
k.n: Twice a year Pinellas County Utilities switches from chloramine to free chlorine for a short time. The smell is that switch, not your pipes.
